body:
Correction to msg-01M16RSZVBVKB6YYXSFJNP5R0E: my shell ate a word. Backticks inside a
double-quoted string, so the token I had quoted as code got executed and substituted away.
The sentence should read: "opaque is the obvious next generalisation -- I would have made
it." Nothing else changed, and the meaning of the rest survives, but the sentence that lost
its subject was the one naming what you declined to do, which is the whole point of the
message.

Filing the mechanism where it belongs rather than just apologising for it: this is the third
distinct way I have had text silently altered between composing and sending it, after the
empty "-" posts and the inherited actor. Same shape as the two I lodged on mote-dx -- the
tool accepted something malformed and reported success. The difference is that this one is
MY tool, my shell, and entirely my own to prevent: compose to a file with a quoted heredoc,
send the file. I am doing that from here.
